grade.first_issue: The first decisive defect is the sine-law equation for triangle ABL. Here θ_L was defined as ∠CAL, whereas the angle at A in triangle ABL is ∠BAL; these are not equal. Thus the denominator sin(α+β+θ_L), and consequently b/c=f(tan β), are unjustified. The analogous step for triangle AKC likewise confuses ∠BAK with ∠KAC. These false inferences replace the central compatibility argument, so Rule E gives a ceiling of 3.
grade.summary: The vector reduction of OM=ON and several preliminary sine-law relations are useful, but the central relation f(tan β)f(tan γ)=1 is derived from incorrect angle identifications. Moreover, the final circumcenter computation is entirely asserted through vague symmetry rather than performed. Correcting the proof requires replacing the central compatibility argument and supplying a substantial calculation, not merely filling a local omission.
strengths: Correctly reduces OM=ON to a linear dot-product identity involving the circumcenter.
Correctly obtains the circumcenter equations 2o·k=|k|² and 2o·l=|l|².
The sine-law formulas for BK in triangle BMK and CL in triangle CNL are valid, and the displayed vector formula for the circumcenter is correct when A,K,L are noncollinear.

errors.description: In triangle ABL the proof substitutes θ_L=∠CAL for ∠BAL, and in triangle AKC it substitutes θ_K=∠BAK for ∠KAC. Hence both side-ratio equations used to obtain the function f are generally false.

The decisive computation of o·(c−b) is omitted. Saying that symmetry and a reciprocal relation 'ensure' the target equality is an unsupported central inference; because the preceding reduction is already invalid, Rule B does not make a score of 4 eligible.

The use of tangent formulas does not address cases in which one of the relevant tangents is undefined or a displayed denominator vanishes; the hypotheses do not establish that these cases are impossible.
